fun_highlights: The vocation arcs (soldier/scholar/maker/wanderer/adrift) genuinely bifurcate lives into different shapes. A soldier life reads structurally differently from a scholar life — a_soldier_service -> m_soldier_ghost -> e_soldier_old is a real three-act arc that no other vocation shares, and the transcripts confirm it: Ren Salvedi's soldier life clusters around w_war_loss, a_soldier_service (going where it's worst), and m_soldier_ghost (carrying it alone), while Iris Brandt's scholar life clusters around a_scholar_question and m_scholar_legacy. This is the game's most effective anti-staleness mechanism.

The callback system earns its keep. cb_lookaway (the child looked away -> midlife -> homeless person) and cb_outcast_return (the yard child, grown) land as genuine long-arc payoffs. In the transcripts, Edmund Ashby's 'made up, to a stranger, for a child he had ignored 47 years before' and Theda Quint's reading the book she kept at age 12 at 55 are the most emotionally resonant moments in the corpus — exactly because they require a memory to have been set.

The era system (war/plague/plenty/hard/turning) successfully varies the world-texture generation to generation. Dynasty 6 (Salvedi) has Ren born into war (w_war_loss, soldier arc intensified), while Dynasty 8 (Ashby) opens in fat years. The era-contextual framings of y_calling and a_marry are particularly good — the war framing of marriage ('the question of marrying has gone, suddenly, from someday to now or perhaps never') is noticeably sharper than the generic pool.

The epitaph/motto crystallization is the game's most satisfying dynasty-layer moment. Seeing 'Nothing was given; all was built' land in the transcript for House Brandt at generation 3, or 'Better a short blaze than a long smoke' for House Salvedi, works as genuine payoff for accumulated play. The anti-repetition logic (USED_MOTTOS, RECENT_CLUSTERS, RECENT_LINES session-wide) is correctly implemented and suppresses the most obvious staleness vector.

Short and early-death lives (Anouk Ashby at 9, Soren Castellane at 18, Liv Quint at 31) create genuine tonal variety and serve as real punctuation marks between longer arcs. 'Gone early, with the better part still ahead' lands harder because the previous dynasty ran 5 generations. The death variance is a structural win.

The 'competing goods' cards (x_honest_or_kind, x_dream_or_duty, x_loyalty_truth) represent genuine moral texture — neither choice is obviously right. These are the most replayable decision moments because they resist mapping: you cannot build a 'correct' strategy around them.
staleness: The childhood checklist is nearly identical across all 15 dynasties: c_origin always fires first, then a near-mandatory rotation through c_unfair (choose burn/shrug), c_book (keep/return), c_wonder or c_friend or c_animal, and c_move or c_dark or c_sibling. Reading the first 10-15 entries of ANY life in the transcript is largely interchangeable. Aldous Renner (D3), Ottilie Mercer (D4), Lazlo Bjornsen (D5), and Annika Okonkwo (D11) all begin with c_unfair -> c_book -> y_mentor -> y_calling within a handful of years of each other. The TRAIT_AFFINITY weighting in engine.js (c_book to 'bookish', c_animal to 'tender', c_wonder to 'dreaming') should differentiate childhoods but the pool is shallow enough that even a non-bookish child hits c_book within a few years.

The 'late love' monoculture has been partially fixed (y_love1 at 16-25 is now the primary nudge) but the transcripts show it still fails. In Dynasty 1, Carys meets love at 46; in Dynasty 6, Anders meets love at 38, marries at 46. In Dynasty 8, Noor meets love at 18, decides No to children at 28, then Yes at 34 (two consecutive child-question draws from a_child). The a_child card with cool:5 and the once-nudge mechanics still cluster many births into the late 30s/early 40s — the 'had a child late' line from latePool appears in at least 8 of 15 dynasties examined.

Certain phrase-level repetition persists across lives despite the freshPick/RECENT_LINES machinery. 'Kept the door and the table open to whoever turned up' appears in Calla Brandt (D1 gen5), Noor Ashby (D8), Yara Okonkwo (D11 gen3) — all from t_warm. 'Left people gentler than they found them' is the epitaph for Anders Salvedi (D6) and Noor Ashby (D8). 'Taught what they knew, and so outlived the knowing of it' appears for Lazlo Bjornsen (D5) and Linnea Okonkwo (D11 gen2). The session-wide RECENT_LINES buffer (150 items) is too large to prevent cross-dynasty recurrence of a small hot pool.

The observation layer (observe() in engine.js) fires the same landmark lines in the same positions across nearly every life: a vit<35 observation somewhere in midlife ('The stairs have started to ask a question of them'), a means_hi line when wealth is accumulated, a spirit_hi line for content characters. Reading the transcript, these ambient beats are structurally indistinguishable between lives — Iris Brandt has 'She has, at last, the particular freedom of not having to think about it' at 88 means (age 41), Cyrus Ashby has 'He has crossed into the quiet country where the bills simply get paid' at similar stats, and so on. The observation pools are deep (10 variants each) but the TRIGGER PATTERN is identical.

The e_bequest / e_legacy / e_craft / e_body elder cluster fires in nearly every long life, in recognizable order. By the time a player has run 4-5 long lives, the elder act has a predictable shape: body card, legacy card, bequest card, craft or peace card. Ronja Brandt (D1 gen4), Greta Ashby (D2 gen3), Anders Salvedi (D6), Noor Ashby (D8) — all hit this same four-beat elder act. The onceDyn cooldowns are set to 3-5 generations but within a single dynasty run these elder beats are essentially guaranteed.

The a_marry logline pool causes textural repetition: 'Married X in front of the few who mattered, and let the world find out after' appears for Henrik Brandt (D1 gen3), Linnea Salvedi (D6 gen3), and Ottilie Quint (D12 gen2). The late-marriage pool is smaller (6 variants) and 'Married X with grey already coming in, and found the promise none the lighter for it' appears for Noor Ashby and Junia Calloway in the same session. Because a_marry is one of the most reliably-drawn cards, its logline repetition is highly visible.

improvements.what: Add 2-3 childhood 'shape' archetypes that replace the default checklist — a child who never had c_unfair because they grew up protected (high seat), a child skips c_book entirely because their era is 'hard' (survival first), a child raised on the motto who faces c_motto_test early. Right now c_origin varies the opening line but the next 8 draws are essentially the same pool regardless of era, seat, or traits.
improvements.why: The childhood checklist is the single most visible replay staleness. A player who has run 5 dynasties can predict the first 15 years of any new life. Structural differentiation here compounds forward because childhood flags (child_books, kept_stray, looked_away) gate the entire callback arc — so varied childhoods produce varied adult payoffs.

improvements.what: Shrink the RECENT_LINES session buffer from 150 to 40-50, and add a per-cluster cap so that any single cluster (e.g. 'teacher', 'kind', 'warm') can appear at most once in the last 8 epitaphs across the entire session. The current 150-item buffer prevents immediate duplication but 'Left people gentler than they found them' and 'Taught what they knew' both recur within the 15-dynasty corpus because their clusters are easy to earn.
improvements.why: Epitaphs are the most memorable single line per life — the player reads them at the death screen and again in the constellation. Repeated epitaphs are the highest-visibility staleness signal in a cross-dynasty session. A tighter cross-dynasty cap here pays outsized dividends.

improvements.what: Add a 'life-shape' gating to the elder act so that e_bequest, e_legacy, and e_peace cannot ALL fire in the same life. Currently every long life hits all three within 15 years of each other, producing an identical 3-beat closing act. Force a draw: if e_legacy fired, e_peace requires onceDyn:2 (skip a generation); or gate e_bequest on having children AND having made a meaningful earlier choice (not just being in the elder stage). The goal is elder acts that are different shapes — some end on the legacy beat, some on the peace beat, some on the craft handoff.
improvements.why: The elder act currently reads as a template. A replay-focused player will notice by their third long life that the closing act is predictable. Differentiating the possible elder endings would restore the 'one more life' pull for experienced players.

improvements.what: Add 4-6 new vocation-specific adult callbacks that reach back to the calling moment more concretely. The scholar arc has cb_study_pays (good) and m_scholar_legacy, but no moment that specifically remembers the age of chose_study and the lean years. A card like 'The dull paid work taken at 22 — the one that fed the questioning years — is still there, still available, and still beneath you' for a scholar who took the paid-work fork at a_scholar_question would create a much richer life-specific arc. The wanderer and adrift arcs are the most underserved here.
improvements.why: The callback system is the game's best anti-staleness mechanism. More callbacks per vocation arc means lives with the same calling still diverge based on which fork within the arc was taken. Currently soldier/scholar/maker have 3 arc cards each; wanderer has 2; adrift has 3 but they fire late and feel generic.

improvements.what: The a_marry logline pool for non-late marriages has 10 variants but 3 of them ('in front of the few who mattered', 'without ceremony and without a single doubt', 'with borrowed rings and no money') are stylistically near-identical (quiet/small ceremony framing). Replacing 2-3 with tonally distinct variants — a marriage that was contentious, one that felt like a business arrangement that became love, one that surprised both of them — would reduce the 'all marriages feel the same' effect in a long session.
improvements.why: a_marry is one of the highest-frequency cards in the game — most lives that reach adulthood draw it. Even small logline variety here is amplified across many plays. The current pool skews heavily toward 'quiet and small and earnest' which is a single emotional register.

verdict: A Life is a well-crafted meditative sim with genuine structural variety — the vocation arcs, callback system, and era layer all work — but it shows its template within 4-5 long lives. The childhood years are the most repetitive section (nearly every life hits c_unfair -> c_book -> y_calling in recognizable order), the elder act is a predictable three-beat closing sequence, and cross-dynasty phrase repetition is higher than the RECENT_LINES system suppresses. The 'one more run' itch is real for the first 3-4 dynasties, driven by the callback payoffs and the motto crystallization, but erodes noticeably by dynasty 6-8 as the machine's seams become legible. A focused pass on childhood structural divergence and elder-act shape variety would push this toward a 7.5 — the bones are strong enough to support it.
